notes: Twelve of thirteen pass on substance, not surface: citations verified against the fixture, the counterfactual was actually executed in scratchpad copies, and the root cause is correctly placed at write-time normalization with the == compare demoted to proximate cause. The one failure is structural: the headline is spread over five sentences instead of the one the skill's fix.md demands, so a skimmer reading only first sentences gets the root cause but not what broke or the fix. Eval critique: assertions 3, 5, 10 and 11 check shape (numbered list, labels present) and would pass a plausible-but-wrong chain; assertion 6 is the discriminating one and should stay. Nothing checks that the chain's citations are accurate or that the counterfactual was actually run rather than asserted, which I verified by hand here; an assertion like 'transcript shows the repro test executed against a patched copy' would close that. The skim-test assertion bundles two checks (one-sentence headline, section leads) so a report can fail it on either, which makes run-to-run comparison noisy; splitting it would help. Run-specific noise: the skill snapshot path did not exist at start and the agent began from a byte-identical older snapshot before switching mid-run, so this run is not a clean measurement of rca-new alone.
